#### 1. juvenile-onset diabetes mellitus-central and peripheral neurodegeneration syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.442)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-381038)

**Proposed mechanism:** Tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (HGNC:11770) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0000422); Lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal damage (HP:0002180); DnaJ Heat Shock Protein Family Member C3 (HGNC:18970) —DISRUPTS→ ER stress response (GO:0034996); ER stress response (GO:0034996) —DECREASES→ Lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0000422); Lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002180); Lysosomal protein degradation (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ Diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005041). Loss-of-function mutations in TPP1 impair lysosomal protein degradation, leading to neuronal damage in NCL2. In juvenile-onset diabetes mellitus-central and peripheral neurodegeneration syndrome, mutations in DNAJC3 disrupt the ER stress response, which in turn negatively impacts lysosomal function, contributing to both neurodegeneration and diabetes mellitus.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstrating that mutations in TPP1 do not lead to impaired lysosomal protein degradation, or that DNAJC3 mutations do not affect lysosomal function in a way that exacerbates neurodegeneration or diabetes. _(variant: rs743474074)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of lysosomal protein degradation in both NCL2 and juvenile-onset diabetes mellitus-central and peripheral neurodegeneration syndrome could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies targeting lysosomal dysfunction for both conditions. For example, enhancing lysosomal clearance pathways or mitigating ER stress might offer benefits.

#### 2. Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, kyphoscoliotic type, 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-381038)

**Proposed mechanism:** TPP1 (HGNC:11770) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal degradation (GO:0005764); lysosomal degradation (GO:0005764) —DECREASES→ abnormal protein aggregates (CHEBI:16795); abnormal protein aggregates (CHEBI:16795) —LEADS_TO→ neurodegeneration (HP:0002188); FKBP14 (HGNC:26815) —DISRUPTS→ proteasomal degradation (GO:0000422); proteasomal degradation (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ connective tissue defects (HP:0002705); lysosomal degradation (GO:0005764) —LEADS_TO→ cellular protein homeostasis (GO:0006464); proteasomal degradation (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ cellular protein homeostasis (GO:0006464). Loss-of-function mutations in TPP1 impair lysosomal degradation, leading to the accumulation of abnormal protein aggregates and neurodegeneration in NCL2. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in FKBP14 disrupt proteasomal degradation, resulting in connective tissue defects in kyphoscoliotic EDS. Both pathways converge on the broader cellular protein homeostasis network, suggesting a shared vulnerability in managing protein quality control.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the lysosomal and proteasomal degradation pathways are entirely independent and do not share any common regulatory factors or downstream effectors relevant to the specific protein aggregates or cellular components affected in each disease. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in TPP1 or FKBP14 in the general population that do not segregate with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the overlap in cellular protein processing defects could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative and connective tissue disorders, potentially involving modulators of lysosomal or proteasomal function.

#### 3. polycystic kidney disease 6 with or without polycystic liver disease  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.397)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-381038)

**Proposed mechanism:** TPP1 (HGNC:11739) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal degradation of proteins (GO:0005741); lysosomal degradation of proteins (GO:0005741) —LEADS_TO→ neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (HP:0002370); DNAJB11 (HGNC:27994) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal degradation of proteins (GO:0005741); lysosomal degradation of proteins (GO:0005741) —LEADS_TO→ polycystic kidney disease (HP:0000010). Mutations in TPP1 disrupt lysosomal degradation of proteins, leading to neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis. Similarly, mutations in DNAJB11 are implicated in polycystic kidney disease, likely through disruption of protein homeostasis pathways that intersect with lysosomal function.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies demonstrate that mutations in TPP1 and DNAJB11 do not converge on shared cellular pathways involved in protein degradation, particularly within the lysosomal system, this hypothesis would be falsified. Specifically, if TPP1's role is solely in substrate cleavage within the lysosome and DNAJB11's role is entirely independent of lysosomal function, the proposed overlap would be incorrect. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of TPP1 and DNAJB11 that are not associated with either disease would weaken the link, although this is less likely for rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role in protein degradation pathways could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis and polycystic kidney disease. Strategies aimed at enhancing protein clearance or lysosomal function might offer cross-disease benefits.

#### 4. cataract 41  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.390)

The shared convergence point is the disruption of normal protein turnover within the lysosome, impacting both neuronal function and lens clarity.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the genetic defect in Cataract 41 does not involve any component of the lysosomal-autophagy pathway or that the accumulated undegraded material in NCL2 does not physically interact with or affect lens crystallin homeostasis. _(variant: Identification of common, benign variants in TPP1 or the putative Cataract 41 gene in affected populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could inform therapeutic strategies for both NCL2 and Cataract 41.
